Services

From the brief to the results

I work as a creative director who also makes the work: the concept, the look and the script, then the edit and every version a campaign needs. One person from the first idea to the final file.

Concept & direction

Creative direction

Setting the look, tone and pace a brand's video should have, then holding every piece to it. Agreed with you before anything is cut, so the first draft is already heading the right way.

Concepts & campaign ideas

The idea a video or a whole campaign is built on, pitched as a few clear routes with references, so you choose a direction before anything is made.

Audience & message

Who the video is for, what they need to believe by the end, and what should make them act. Settled before the script, so every scene has a job.

Script writing

Writing the through-line: the voiceover, the on-screen text, the order the story gets told in. Written against the material you have rather than the material you wish you had.

Casting & directing voiceover actors

Casting the voice or the spokesperson, briefing and directing them through the session, then cutting the read into the edit. You hear the options before anyone is booked.

Consultation calls

A call to talk through what you already have and what it needs to become. Bring the footage, the brief, or just the problem, and you leave knowing what is possible and what it will take.

Production & post

Video editing

I build the story out of the material and find the pace that holds it together. Rough cut first, so the shape is agreed before anyone spends time on polish.

Visual effects

Taking out what should not be in frame, adding what should, and the quiet fixes nobody is meant to notice. Screen replacements, clean-up, tracking.

Animated elements & motion graphics

Titles, lower-thirds, logo animation, charts, and light 2D work when a scene needs it. Built to your brand rather than out of a template.

Color grading & correction

Matching every shot so the piece reads as one film, then grading it to sit with your brand. Material from different cameras or different days is the normal case, not a problem.

Sound design & mixing

Cleaning up dialogue, placing effects, balancing music, and mixing to broadcast and streaming levels. Poor sound is what makes a video feel cheap.

Licensed music & stock footage

Finding the track, and the shots that fill the gaps, then clearing the license so it is safe to publish anywhere. I work from paid premium libraries, so the choice is not limited to whatever happens to be free, and the paperwork comes with the files.

Campaigns & growth

Case study & results videos

Turning what you did for a client into a story: the problem, the work, and the numbers in clear graphics. The video that helps win the next client.

Campaign cut-downs

One set of material turned into everything a campaign needs: the main spot, square and vertical cuts, short hooks for paid social, each edited for where it runs rather than resized.

Ad versions for testing

Several versions of an ad with different openings, lengths or calls to action, so you can see which one performs instead of guessing.

Social content plans

What a brand posts and when, planned from the material you already have, so one shoot keeps feeding your channels for weeks.

Brand video guidelines

A short reference for how the brand's videos look, sound and move, so every future piece stays consistent, whoever makes it.

Subtitling

Subtitles timed to be read rather than merely transcribed, and full language versions in English, Portuguese and Spanish.

Capacity

One person, and what that means for your deadline

One person, no team, no account managers. That is the arrangement, and these are the parts of it that affect a deadline.

Series work is normal
Eighteen training videos for one client. A nine-lesson course. A campaign that went out as a thirty-second spot, a sixty-second square cut and five vertical reels, all from one set of material.
Nothing is relayed twice
Your notes go to the person making the change. There is no account manager translating a brief, and no version of the conversation you are not part of.
You hear about a clash early
I take on a limited number of projects at a time. If your date does not fit, you hear it on the first call rather than three weeks in.
For Creators

YouTube editing built for retention

I run a video essay channel of my own, The Cat's Pajamas, so I edit YouTube from the inside: what keeps people watching past the first thirty seconds, and what makes them click in the first place.

Hooks and pacing
The first seconds decide whether anyone stays. The opening and the rhythm are cut around where viewers drop off, not the order things were filmed in.
Packaging
Title and thumbnail ideas that fit the video, worked out while editing it rather than afterwards.
A steady schedule
Weekly or monthly uploads on a retainer, so the channel keeps moving without you editing at midnight.
